builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
summary: The method replaces pointwise hypothesis testing (a claim h against its complement) with a contrast set of mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive competing explanations that the agent scores by how evidence redistributes belief across the set. The cost is low in infrastructure terms since it changes only the unit an LLM agent proposes and scores, but it adds design complexity: constructing valid contrast sets requires domain knowledge to ensure explanations are genuinely exclusive and exhaustive. It can fail when the true explanation is omitted from the set, when belief concentrates prematurely on a wrong alternative, or in domains where exhaustive competitor enumeration is impractical.
rationale: The technique is API-compatible and cheap to trial, but its reported gains come from six specific scientific domains, so the reader should validate it on their own hypothesis-evaluation workloads before production adoption.
technique: Contrast sets for hypothesis evaluation in discovery agents

claims.statement: The method replaces pointwise hypothesis testing (a claim h against its complement) with a contrast set of mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive competing explanations that the agent scores by how evidence redistributes belief across the set. The cost is low in infrastructure terms since it changes only the unit an LLM agent proposes and scores, but it adds design complexity: constructing valid contrast sets requires domain knowledge to ensure explanations are genuinely exclusive and exhaustive. It can fail when the true explanation is omitted from the set, when belief concentrates prematurely on a wrong alternative, or in domains where exhaustive competitor enumeration is impractical.
Contrast sets resolve 67% more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget, and resolve 73% of rejected pointwise candidates to a specific alternative on the same evidence.
